question: To protect one-horned rhinos from poachers which state has launched the Operation Falcon in August 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Falcon** was launched by the state of **Assam** in **August 2025** to protect the **one-horned rhinos**, a species that is critically endangered and endemic to the Indian subcontinent. 
 
• **Assam** is home to the **Kaziranga National Park**, which is globally renowned for its population of one-horned rhinos and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The initiative aims to combat **poaching activities** that threaten the survival of this iconic species. Poachers target these rhinos primarily for their horns, which are highly valued in illegal wildlife markets.
 
• **Operation Falcon** involves multiple stakeholders, including local government agencies, forest officials, wildlife experts, and law enforcement authorities, to ensure the comprehensive protection of rhinos.
 
• Assam's government has also employed advanced technologies such as **drone surveillance**, **GPS tracking**, and **anti-poaching camps** under Operation Falcon to strengthen conservation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **One-Horned Rhinos:**

 
 
• The **Indian rhinoceros**, commonly known as the one-horned rhinoceros, is primarily found in northeastern India and Nepal.
 
• It is listed as **vulnerable** on the **IUCN Red List**, with Assam being one of its last remaining habitats.
 
• Rhino horns are composed of **keratin**, the same protein that makes up human nails and hair, and are falsely believed to have medicinal properties, driving illegal trade.
 
 
 
• **Kaziranga National Park:**
 
 
• Located in **Assam**, Kaziranga National Park is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a critical habitat for one-horned rhinos.
 
• The park is renowned for its **success in rhino conservation**, housing approximately **2,400 rhinos** as per recent census data.
 
• Kaziranga also supports a wide range of biodiversity, including species like tigers, elephants, swamp deer, and wild water buffalo.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Poaching Measures:**
 
 
• Over the years, Assam has intensified its **anti-poaching efforts** by forming **dedicated task forces**, establishing **anti-poaching camps**, and adopting modern technologies like drones and thermal imaging cameras.
 
• Local communities are actively involved in conservation efforts, providing surveillance and reporting suspicious activities.
 
• International collaborations, such as partnerships with the **WWF** and **TRAFFIC**, have further supported rhino protection.
 
 
 
• **Other Rhino Habitats in India:**
 
 
• Besides Assam, one-horned rhinos are found in **Manas National Park**, **Orang National Park**, and **Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary has one of the highest densities of rhinos in India despite being much smaller in size compared to Kaziranga.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rhino Census:** Assam conducts periodic rhino censuses to monitor population trends and assess the success of conservation efforts.
 
• **Kaziranga National Park Floods:** The park faces annual floods due to the Brahmaputra River, which impacts wildlife but also regenerates the ecosystem.
 
• **Global Rhino Conservation:** International efforts, including the **Rhino Impact Bond** and campaigns by **Save the Rhino International**, contribute to rhino protection worldwide.
 
• **Rhino Conservation Challenges:** Key challenges include habitat loss, human-wildlife conflict, and the growing demand for rhino horns in Asian markets.
